newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU cannot rule out single taxes under EMU.
newsitem.headline: EU cannot rule out single taxes under EMU.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it could not rule out the possiblity of some form of tax harmonisation among countries joining a common currency.

Responding to a report in Britain's newspaper The Independent that France and Germany were secretly preparing plans for a single tax system, a Commission official said: "I don't exclude that possiblity...It is intellectually plausible."

The official cautioned, however, that it was wrong to interpret such a potential development as a further condition for qualification in economic and monetary union (EMU), a suggestion implied in the newspaper's article.
"This isn't a new set of conditions that you must necessarily sign up to," he added.
Both France and Germany denied on Thursday that they were leading a quiet effort to create a single European tax system.

Commission officials stressed that at a summit of EU leaders in Dublin last month there was considerable discussion over the idea of flexibility -- a policy that would allow certain countries in the 15-nation bloc to forge ahead faster in certain areas than others.
Within this context it was conceivable that a common form of taxation among those joining EMU would be considered as a viable option.
Indeed, the drive towards tax harmonisation across the EU has been a subject of discussions among finance ministers for years, often with less than spectacular results.
Officials said Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy is expected to put forward a paper on the subject of flexiblity in fiscal policy matters under EMU in the next few weeks.
